title: A stenosis detector was tested on an external coronary angiography cohort
summary: A learned detector using coronary-vessel features achieved AP@50 of 0.434 on 48 angiography images from 27 Oxford Acute Myocardial Infarction study patients. Test-time augmentation raised it to 0.480. Standard YOLOv11-L scored 0.339 without augmentation. These are lesion-localization scores from a small retrospective cohort.
ai_technology: Fusion-YOLOv11-L; UNet++; learned vessel segmentation and lesion detection
organization: University of Oxford; Oxford University Hospitals NHS Trust

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 date, Methods §2.1–2.4 and external test results, especially Table 5

evidence.tested: The study trained and tuned the model on ARCADE-derived data and assessed localization of 85 stenoses on separately sourced OxAMI frames.
evidence.unknown: The result covers selected end-diastolic frames and a small external sample. Patient-level diagnostic performance and clinical outcomes were outside this evaluation.
evidence.ai_role: Fusion-YOLOv11-L combined learned coronary-vessel segmentation features and lesion detection features to localize stenoses in angiography frames.
